claims.text: The uncoated (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 alloy has a large magnetocaloric response.
The uncoated (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 alloy has a large barocaloric response.
The uncoated alloy has poor load-bearing integrity and initiates surface cracks under operational conditions.
The proposed intervention is a roughly 10 μm Ni-P coating electrodeposited at room temperature.
Heating the coated material at 300°C for 30 minutes will ensure strong coating–substrate adhesion.
The treatment will produce a continuous, well-adhered, ductile Ni-P surface layer.
The Ni-P layer will absorb and redistribute surface mechanical stresses.
Stress absorption and redistribution by the Ni-P layer will suppress crack initiation.
The Ni-P layer will inhibit crack propagation.
Applying the coating and low-temperature heat treatment will leave the alloy's bulk caloric phase unchanged.
The bulk phase of the alloy is responsible for its large caloric response.
The coated alloy will have greater fracture toughness than the uncoated alloy.
The coated alloy will have greater load-bearing capacity than the uncoated alloy.
The coated alloy will exhibit significantly less crack initiation than the uncoated alloy.
The coated alloy will retain caloric entropy changes and sharp phase transitions comparable to those of the uncoated alloy under magnetic-field operation.
The coated alloy will retain caloric entropy changes and sharp phase transitions comparable to those of the uncoated alloy under pressure-field operation.
The proposed benefits apply near 300 K, at magnetic fields of approximately 1–2 T, pressures around 0.5 GPa, and mechanical loads below the base alloy's yield limit.
The intervention is not claimed to remain effective under high-cycle fatigue beyond the stated operating ranges.
